claims.statement: Git is a policy-free git command runner plus one identity invariant: StartAsync first runs EnsureRepositoryAsync, which throws InvalidOperationException unless `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` equals IHostEnvironment.ContentRootPath and `git remote get-url origin` parses into a RepositoryIdentity; the parsed identity is stored in Git.Repository and is the only later proof of the clone's identity.

RepositoryIdentity.Parse handles three remote shapes with no git library: it trims whitespace and a trailing slash, strips a case-insensitive `.git` suffix, then uses `Uri.AbsolutePath` when the value contains `://` or everything after the first `:` for scp-like forms, and returns the last two path segments as owner and name — returning null for blank, colon-less, or fewer-than-two-segment values, so deeper paths collapse to the last two segments.

SyncMainAsync has exactly two call sites: Git.StartAsync under a linked CancellationTokenSource with CancelAfter of ten seconds, and GitHubWebhookProcessor.ProcessPushWebhookAsync, which awaits it inline inside the webhook request; the three-argument overload returns immediately for a deleted ref or any ref other than exactly `refs/heads/main`, so issue-branch pushes never update the mirror and there is no periodic fetch.

The sync path is fetch `--prune origin`, then FindMirrorProblemAsync, then `rev-list --count main..origin/main` with a zero-count early return, then `merge --ff-only origin/main` bracketed by rev-parse before/after; it catches InvalidOperationException (logged as a warning) and OperationCanceledException (logged at Debug), so a dirty mirror, unreachable remote, or the ten-second bound never fails startup or a webhook delivery.

FindMirrorProblemAsync returns a reason string for exactly three states, in order: not checked out on `main` (Ordinal comparison), uncommitted tracked changes detected via `status --porcelain --untracked-files=no`, and local commits ahead of origin/main via `rev-list --count origin/main..main`; the `--untracked-files=no` flag is required because the gitignored `.sebastian/` worktrees live inside the clone and would otherwise make the mirror permanently dirty.

The same FindMirrorProblemAsync result is handled asymmetrically: the sync path logs and skips, while ImplementSpec.PrepareWorkspaceAsync throws InvalidOperationException for a mirror problem, an issue owner/repository that does not match the parsed origin (OrdinalIgnoreCase), or a null Git.Repository (hosted service not started) — because starting an agent from an unreviewed base has no safe degraded mode.

PrepareLock is a static SemaphoreSlim(1,1) shared by every ImplementSpec instance across DI scopes, acquired before and released in a finally around the whole preparation including the fetch and fast-forward, so concurrent jobs cannot interleave mirror-rewriting operations; it is not a repository-wide lock, because once preparation returns the agent works in its own worktree with its own branch and index.

Per-issue workspaces are `<git.Root>/.sebastian/workspaces/<issueNumber>` on branch `sebastian/issue-<n>`; if the directory already exists it is returned unchanged (the previous run's uncommitted agent work must not be deleted), and only when it is missing does preparation run `worktree prune` then `worktree add -B <branch> <path> main` from local main, where `-B` re-points a leftover branch ref instead of failing.

Preparation deliberately does not serialize against the push-webhook sync, which takes no semaphore: a documented shortcut accepts that a concurrent `merge --ff-only` and `worktree add` can collide on `.git/index.lock`, in which case the losing job fails with an InvalidOperationException while the repository stays consistent.

The git layer never commits, pushes, creates pull requests, or resolves conflicts — its entire verb set is fetch, merge --ff-only, worktree add/prune, status, rev-parse, rev-list, remote get-url, and branch --show-current — and the prohibition is stated independently in ImplementationAgent's fixed Instructions and in ImplementSpec.BuildPrompt, with a shell deny-list covering only the destructive subset.

The runner spawns `git` via ProcessStartInfo with an argument list and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, throws InvalidOperationException carrying stderr on any non-zero exit, and kills the whole process tree on cancellation before rethrowing the OperationCanceledException.

Because nothing is committed, `.sebastian/workspaces` is the system's only durable artifact store: deleting it destroys all agent output irrecoverably, and a successful run's only record is the source-generated log line that includes the worktree path, `git -C <worktree> status --short`, and the agent response text.

Test coverage of this area is asymmetric: ImplementSpecTests drives PrepareWorkspaceAsync against a real temporary bare-origin clone (TestRepository) and pins worktree reuse with uncommitted work preserved, recreation after `git worktree remove --force`, dirty-main rejection, and foreign-repository rejection, while SyncMainAsync has no test at all — neither the ref filter, the behind-count short-circuit, nor the swallow-on-failure behavior.

None of the git behavior is configurable: both refs are hardcoded constants `Git.BaseBranch = "main"` and `Git.BaseRef = "origin/main"`, and there is no git section in SebastianConfig, so a repository whose default branch is not `main` cannot be served without a code change.

Git derives its working root once in the constructor from IHostEnvironment.ContentRootPath (full-pathed, trailing separator trimmed), exposes it as Git.Root, and uses it as the WorkingDirectory of every spawned git process; the startup invariant compares git rev-parse --show-toplevel against that stored root via PathEquals.

Every Git verb funnels into one private RunAsync that passes arguments as a discrete ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList with no shell, no window and no stdin redirection, sets GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 on the child environment so credential or host-key prompts fail fast, and surfaces git's stderr inside the InvalidOperationException message.

On cancellation RunAsync kills the entire git process tree with Kill(entireProcessTree: true) before rethrowing the OperationCanceledException, and TryKill ignores InvalidOperationException because the process may already have exited.

PrepareWorkspaceAsync acquires the static PrepareLock as its very first await, before the git.Repository null check and the owner/name comparison, so serialization covers the identity cross-check, the fetch, the mirror guard, the fast-forward and the worktree add/prune; the lock is released in a finally.

The owner/repository cross-check against Git.Repository uses OrdinalIgnoreCase and runs before any fetch, so a foreign issue event is rejected without spawning a git subprocess; the only network and worktree work happens after it passes.

Worktree reuse is decided purely on Directory.Exists of <clone>/.sebastian/workspaces/<issue>, not on git's worktree bookkeeping: when the directory exists the path is returned untouched so the previous run's uncommitted agent work survives, and only a missing directory leads to worktree prune plus worktree add -B.

FindMirrorProblemAsync runs its three guards in order — current branch is exactly main (Ordinal), no tracked changes via status --porcelain --untracked-files=no, and no commits ahead in origin/main..main — returning null only when all pass.

The two SyncMainAsync call sites are Git.StartAsync under a linked CancellationTokenSource bounded by CancelAfter(10s) and GitHubWebhookProcessor.ProcessPushWebhookAsync, which awaits the sync inline inside the webhook request; there is no periodic fetch.

Program.cs registers Git through a factory and then registers the same resolved instance as IHostedService, which is what lets every job see the singleton whose Repository and Root were initialized during StartAsync.

TestRepository.Create builds a real temporary repository for these tests — git init --bare --initial-branch=main, clone over a file:// URL, seeded README.md pushed to origin — and CreateGit wires Git to a TestHostEnvironment over the working clone, so every ImplementSpecTests case must call git.StartAsync to populate Git.Repository.

When a job's preparation throws, JobQueue catches the exception in its per-job handler, logs 'Job {Key} failed' at Error, and removes the in-flight key in a finally, so a retry requires another qualifying event.

No test exercises SyncMainAsync at all — its ref filter, behind-count short-circuit, swallow-on-failure behavior and ten-second bound are unverified — while FindMirrorProblemAsync is only covered indirectly through RejectsDirtyMain, and the 'Git repository is not initialized' throw is never reached because every test starts the hosted service first.

Worktree reuse preserves work that was never committed, so deleting .sebastian/ (gitignored and inside the clone) permanently destroys a run's only output: nothing in git history or in code can reconstruct it.

The accepted index.lock race exists because PrepareLock serializes only job preparation: the push-webhook SyncMainAsync runs on a request thread without the semaphore, so a concurrent merge --ff-only and worktree add can collide and the losing job fails with an InvalidOperationException while the repository stays consistent.

The agent's no-git rule is layered: ImplementationAgent's instructions and ImplementSpec.BuildPrompt both forbid git commands, and a shell deny-list blocks the destructive subset \bgit\s+(push|reset|clean|checkout\s+--)\b, leaving commit unenforced by the host.
